paper.title_en: Charge-even full counting statistics and directed thermal spin transport in interacting conductors
paper.abstract_en: A vanishing charge current does not imply symmetric charge-transfer fluctuations. We identify a stronger nonequilibrium regime in which directed thermal spin transport coexists with an exactly charge-even finite-time transfer distribution, $P_t(N_c,N_s)=P_t(-N_c,N_s)$. A canonical involution combining particle-hole conjugation, spin reversal, channel exchange, and energy reflection pairs every transfer history $(N_c,N_s)$ with $(-N_c,N_s)$. Consequently, all joint cumulants with odd charge order vanish identically, while the spin current and even charge noise can remain finite. We establish the result for interacting finite systems under explicit Hamiltonian and preparation conditions and derive its exact long-time continuum counterpart at arbitrary tunnel broadening. Interacting finite-lead dynamics, a complete thermal trace, and a sequential-tunneling description confirm the transport signal, distributional symmetry, and controlled breakdown under detuning or filter mismatch. The resulting hierarchy of null relations provides a substantially stronger diagnostic of spin-charge separation than $J_c=0$.
